en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, both from Hafs—Abu Bakr said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sulaym, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: I saw the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) squatting on his heels (muq'iyan) eating dates.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi and 'Abdullah ibn 'Awn al-Hilali narrated to us—Yahya said: "informed us," and Ibn 'Awn said: "narrated to us"—Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) eating cucumbers with fresh ripe dates.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to me, Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, both from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration, and neither of them doubted about casting the date-stones between the two fingers.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Khumayr, from 'Abdullah ibn Busr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came as a guest to my father. He said: So we presented to him food and watbah (a dish of dates, curd, and butter), and he ate from it. Then dates were brought to him, and he began eating them and casting the stones between his two fingers, joining the index finger and the middle finger—Shu'bah said: "It is my presumption, and it is in it, if Allah wills: casting the stones between the two fingers"—then a drink was brought, so he drank it and passed it to the one on his right. He said: Then my father took the reins of his riding beast and said: "Supplicate to Allah for us." So he said: "O Allah, bless them in what You have provided them, forgive them, and have mercy upon them."

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me, both from 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani and 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas ibn Malik, that a tailor invited the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he added: Thabit said: I heard Anas say: "Afterward, no food was ever prepared for me where gourd could possibly be put into it except that it was put into it."

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: A man invited the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so I went along with him. Soup containing gourd was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) began eating of that gourd and it pleased him. He said: When I saw that, I began putting pieces of gourd toward him and not eating any of it myself. Anas said: "Ever since, gourd has continued to please me."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas—in what was recited to him—from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: A tailor invited the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to a meal he had prepared. Anas ibn Malik said: I went along with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to that meal. He served the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) barley bread and soup containing gourd and cured meat (qadid). Anas said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) following the pieces of gourd around the edges of the dish. He said: Ever since that day, I have always loved gourd.

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Harb ibn Maymun narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), concerning the meal of Abu Talhah, something similar to their hadith.

Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, Usamah informed me that Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah narrated to him that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: I came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) one day and found him sitting with his Companions talking to them, having bound his stomach with a band—Usamah said: and I doubt whether it was over a stone. I said to some of his Companions: "Why has the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) bound his stomach?" They said: "From hunger." So I went to Abu Talhah, who was the husband of Umm Sulaym bint Milhan, and said: "O father! I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) having bound his stomach with a band, and I asked some of his Companions and they said: 'From hunger.'" Abu Talhah entered upon my mother and said: "Is there anything?" She said: "Yes, I have some pieces of bread and dates; if the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) comes to us alone, we can satisfy him, but if someone else comes with him, it will be too little for them." Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith with its story.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard Jarir ibn Zayd narrating from 'Amr ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Abu Talhah saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) lying down in the mosque tossing and turning from back to stomach. He went to Umm Sulaym and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) lying down in the mosque tossing and turning from back to stomach, and I think he is hungry." And he related the hadith, saying therein: "Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), Abu Talhah, Umm Sulaym, and Anas ibn Malik ate, and there remained leftovers, which we gifted to our neighbors."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Bajali narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Musa narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah narrated to me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this hadith, and he said therein: "Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ate, and the people of the household ate, and they left over what they could send to their neighbors."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Yahya, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, with this story concerning the food of Abu Talhah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he said therein: Abu Talhah stood at the door until the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived, and said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, it was only a little bit of food." He said: "Bring it forward, for Allah will surely place blessing in it."

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Raqqi narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Abu Talhah ordered Umm Sulaym to prepare food specifically for the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) himself, and then sent me to him... and he related the hadith, saying therein: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) placed his hand upon it and mentioned the Name of Allah over it, then said: "Admit ten." So he admitted them, and they entered. He said: "Eat and mention the Name of Allah." So they ate, until he did that for eighty men. Then the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and the people of the household ate after that, and they left leftovers.

Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to me, my father narrated to me, Sa'd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah sent me to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he related the hadith in the manner of the hadith of Ibn Numayr, except that he said at its end: "Then he took what remained, gathered it, and prayed for blessing in it—he said—and it returned to what it had been. Then he said: 'Take this.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his—my father narrated to us, Sa'd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: Abu Talhah sent me to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to invite him, having prepared some food. He said: I came while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was with the people. He looked at me, so I felt shy and said: "Answer Abu Talhah's invitation." He said to the people: "Stand up." Abu Talhah said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have only prepared a little food for you." He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) touched it and supplicated for blessing in it, then said: "Admit a group of my Companions, ten of them." And he said: "Eat," and brought out something for them from between his fingers. They ate until they were full and then left. Then he said: "Admit ten." So they ate until they were full. He kept admitting ten and letting ten out until not one of them remained except that he had entered and eaten until full. Then he gathered it together, and behold, it was just as it had been when they first ate from it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik ibn Anas, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah said to Umm Sulaym: "I heard the voice of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sounding weak, and I recognized hunger in it. Do you have anything?" She said: "Yes." She brought out some barley loaves, took a veil of hers and wrapped the bread in part of it, tucked it under my garment, and wrapped me with the rest of it, then sent me to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: I went with it and found the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sitting in the mosque with people around him. I stood near them, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Has Abu Talhah sent you?" I said: "Yes." He said: "With a meal?" I said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to those who were with him: "Stand up." He said: So he set out and I walked ahead of them until I reached Abu Talhah and informed him. Abu Talhah said: "O Umm Sulaym, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has brought the people, and we have nothing to feed them!" She said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: Abu Talhah went out until he met the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) approached with him until they entered. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Bring what you have, O Umm Sulaym." She brought that bread, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered it broken into crumbs. Umm Sulaym squeezed a butter-skin of hers over it to season it. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said over it whatever Allah willed that he say, and then said: "Admit ten." He admitted them, and they ate until they were full, then left. Then he said: "Admit ten." He admitted them, and they ate until they were full, then left. Then he said: "Admit ten," until all the people ate and were full, and the people were seventy or eighty men.

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to me from a written paper that he compared with mine and then recited to me, saying: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, Sa'id ibn Mina' narrated to us, saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: When the Trench (al-Khandaq) was being dug, I saw hunger in the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). So I returned to my wife and said to her: "Do you have anything? For I saw severe hunger in the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." She brought out a bag containing a sa' of barley, and we had a tame young sheep. He said: So I slaughtered it and she ground the barley, finishing when I finished. I cut the meat into pieces in its cooking pot, then turned to go to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). She said: "Do not humiliate me before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and those with him!" He said: I came to him and whispered to him, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, we have slaughtered a young sheep of ours, and my wife has ground a sa' of barley that we had; so come, you and a small group with you." Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out loudly, saying: "O people of the Trench, Jabir has prepared a feast for you, so come welcome!" And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not take down your cooking pot and do not bake your dough until I arrive." So I arrived, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived leading the people, until I entered upon my wife. She said: "May this befall you and that!" I said: "I did what you told me." She brought out our dough for him, and he spat into it and blessed it; then he went to our cooking pot, spat into it and blessed it, then said: "Call another woman to bake with you, and ladle out from your cooking pot, but do not take it off the fire." And they were one thousand people! I swear by Allah, they ate until they left it and went away, while our cooking pot was still boiling as it had been, and our dough—or as al-Dahhak said—was still being baked as it had been!

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me, Abu Hisham—meaning al-Mughirah ibn Salamah—informed us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to us, he said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: While Abu Bakr was sitting and 'Umar was with him, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to them and said: "What caused the two of you to sit here?" They said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, hunger drove us out of our houses." Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Khalaf ibn Khalifah.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went out one day—or night—and unexpectedly met Abu Bakr and 'Umar. He said: "What brought the two of you out of your homes at this hour?" They said: "Hunger, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "And I, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, that which brought the two of you out has brought me out as well; stand up." So they stood up with him. He went to a man from the Ansar, but behold, he was not in his home. When the woman saw him, she said: "Welcome and ease!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to her: "Where is so-and-so?" She said: "He went to fetch fresh water for us." Just then the Ansari man arrived, looked at the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and his two companions, and then said: "Praise be to Allah, no one today has more honorable guests than I!" He said: So he went and brought them a bunch of dates containing unripe dates, dry dates, and fresh ripe dates, and said: "Eat from this." Then he took a knife, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Beware of slaughtering a milch animal." So he slaughtered for them, and they ate from the sheep and from that cluster of dates, and drank. When they were full and had quenched their thirst, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to Abu Bakr and 'Umar: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will surely be asked about this blessing on the Day of Resurrection: hunger drove you out of your homes, and then you did not return until this blessing reached you."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, that a Persian neighbor of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to prepare savory soup. He prepared some for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and then came to invite him. He said: "And this one?"—referring to 'A'ishah. He said: "No." So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "No." He returned to invite him again, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "And this one?" He said: "No." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "No." Then he returned to invite him a third time, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "And this one?" He said: "Yes"—on the third time. So the two of them arose following one another eagerly until they came to his house.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah ibn Abi Rawwad narrated to me, Abu al-Jawwab narrated to us, 'Ammar—who is Ibn Ruzayq—narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir; (H) and Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Abu Mas'ud, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); and from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, with this hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, both from Abu Mu'awiyah; (H) and Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdhami and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated it to us, they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us; (H) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Sufyan; all of them from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Abu Mas'ud, with this hadith from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), in the manner of the hadith of Jarir. Nasr ibn 'Ali said in his narration of this hadith: Abu Usamah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Shaqiq ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari narrated to us... and he related the hadith.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and their wording was similar—they said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: There was a man among the Ansar called Abu Shu'ayb, and he had a slave who was a butcher. He saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and recognized hunger in his face, so he said to his slave: "Woe to you, prepare a meal for us for five persons, for I want to invite the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) as the fifth of five." He said: So he prepared it, then went to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and invited him as the fifth of five. Another man followed them, and when he reached the door, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "This man has followed us; if you wish you may permit him, and if you wish he will return." He said: "No, rather I give him permission, O Messenger of Allah."

Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated it to me, 'Abd al-Rahman—meaning Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us, both saying: Hammad narrated to us, with this chain of narration, except that he said: "and let one of you wipe the dish clean," and he said: "in which part of your food is the blessing, or in which of it you are blessed."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me, Bahz narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "When one of you eats, let him lick his fingers, for he does not know in which of them the blessing lies."

Muhammad ibn Hatim and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' al-'Abdi narrated to me, they said: Bahz narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, that whenever the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ate food, he licked his three fingers. He said: And he said: "When a morsel falls from one of you, let him remove whatever dirt is on it and eat it, and not leave it for Satan." And he commanded us to wipe the dish clean, saying: "For you do not know in which part of your food the blessing lies."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih and Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), mentioning licking; and from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), mentioning the morsel, in the manner of their hadith.

Abu Kurayb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, both from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration: "When a morsel falls from one of you..." to the end of the hadith, and he did not mention the beginning of the hadith: "Indeed Satan is present with one of you..."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Indeed, Satan is present with one of you at everything he does, even being present with him at his meal. So when a morsel falls from one of you, let him remove whatever dirt was on it, then let him eat it and not leave it for Satan. And when he finishes, let him lick his fingers, for indeed he does not know in which part of his food the blessing lies."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari informed us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated it to me, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, both from Sufyan, with this chain of narration, the like of it; and in the hadith of both of them: "and let him not wipe his hand with a cloth until he licks it or gives it to someone to lick it," and what followed it.
